input.title: Verify in production: the executor's between-items hold read, and the invocation drop
input.body:
#1218 made an executor run drain the queue instead of settling one item, and had it re-read the operator hold between items via `GET /repos/{repo}/actions/variables/CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL`. Every part of that is covered by tests that ran — except one thing no test can settle: **whether the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` is allowed to make that read at all.** The workflow `permissions:` block has no key for variables access, and the session that wrote it could not reach `api.github.com` to check the docs, so the code was written to degrade rather than guess: on any non-200 it falls back to the value the run started with and logs the access it lacked. That fallback is correct either way, but which branch actually runs is unknown until a real drain makes the call.

The second read below is the change's own premise — that the invocation count drops — which is only true in production by construction.

```
Original-issue: #1214
In-production-when: a `Claudinite executor` workflow run in missingbulb/Claudinite that started after 2026-08-22T10:25Z (the merge of #1218) has finished, AND its log shows it settled at least one item (a line matching `^- #\d+:` in the run's final summary). The between-items read only happens after a settle, so a run that found nothing pickable proves nothing and does not satisfy this.
Verify: read that run's log. (1) If it contains `could not read CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL live`, the token CANNOT read repository variables: the between-items hold is inert and the operator hold gates run starts only, as it did before #1218 — record the exact status code from the log line, comment it here, and reopen Original-issue so the fallback can be made the documented behaviour (DESIGN §8 already states this outcome as possible; it would become the actual one). If the line is absent, the live read works — comment saying so, quoting the run URL. Either result is a pass: this verification exists to learn which. (2) Count `Claudinite executor` workflow runs in the 24h after the merge and in the 24h before it. Assert the after-count is lower. If it is not, say so with both counts and reopen Original-issue — the change's whole premise is that it is.
Not-before: 2026-08-23T12:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day
Model: sonnet
```

**How to converge this run:**

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the real Actions run list. Never infer it from the merge, a green CI run, or elapsed time.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Comment the evidence you actually read — the run URL, the presence or absence of the log line with its status code, and both run counts — then close this issue as completed. Where a `Verify:` branch above says to reopen `Original-issue:`, do that first and link it from your comment here.
3. **Not yet live** (no qualifying run has settled an item yet) → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, and leave it open. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

input.body:
Both tests in #1219 reddened CI on #1218, whose diff touched neither.

### The rimraf race — fixed at the cause, not at the call site

`ENOTEMPTY` on a temp `.git` has now been closed three times (#235, #258, #1219) and come back twice. The reason is visible in the pattern: each fix repaired the one call site that happened to fail, while every other site kept spelling its own bare `rmSync`. So this moves the retry into **`engine/remove-tree.mjs`**, once, with the whole story of why; the 127 sites that delete a tree call it; and a guard test fails when a new site spells the delete by hand.

The guard is the part that matters — and it earned its keep immediately: my own "files that drive git" heuristic found 13 files, and the guard then found **9 more sites in 2 files** it had missed. `engine-tests/helpers.mjs`'s existing `cleanup()` now delegates to the same helper, so there is one implementation rather than two.

One correction to the issue's framing, from reading the code around the fix: the retry is the **second** line of defense, not the first. #235's real fix was `GIT_ENV` keeping git's auto-gc and maintenance in the foreground so no detached process outlives a fixture command. Both comments now say which is which, so the next reader doesn't mistake the retry for the cure.

### The heartbeat beat — no clock at all

The three beat tests started a 5 ms interval and waited 40 ms of real time for at least 2 beats — 2 of a possible 8, which a loaded runner coalescing timers fails. All three now drive `t.mock.timers`, so the assertion is exact (N intervals ticked ⇒ N beats) instead of probabilistic, and the file runs in 121 ms instead of sleeping through 100 ms of it. A comment says not to reintroduce a real `setTimeout` wait "to give the beat a chance", since that is the bug.

### Proving it

- Reverting `clearInterval` reds 2 of the rewritten beat tests; making the beat never fire reds 2 others.
- Re-introducing one bare `rmSync(..., { recursive: true })` reds the guard, naming the file and line.
- Emptying the guard's own scope reds its companion test — a sweep guard that matches nothing reads green forever otherwise.

The suite caught one real consequence I'd have missed: `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs` is copied into a hand-curated scratch canon by its fixture, so its new import needed a copy line in both fixture builders. That is the fixture doing its job.

Full suite 2543 green; `check_the_work` 0 blocking (after the two pack version bumps and their `VERSIONS.md` rows); `check_the_world` 0 blocking; the consumer rehearsal 40 green across all shapes and both modes.

One advisory left deliberately: `file-placement` flags `vendoring/rehearsal/rehearse.mjs` reaching `engine/remove-tree.mjs` at distance 3. Its own remedy text exempts "a deliberate cross-cutting concern", which a single shared delete is.

Closes #1219
